propers.text:
Concede, quaesumus, omnipotens Deus: ut ad meliorem vitam Sanctorum tuorum
exempla nos provocent; quatenus, quorum solemnia agimus, etiam actus
imitemur. Per Dominum nostrum.

provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: the 1862 carries `Feliee` here, which the CMAA text layer of the 1962 does not; the 1862 reads `D6mine` where the 1962 reads `Domine` (letterforms inferred, not read: the difference is at the level of the recogniser); the 1862 supplies the saint's name as `Felicis M rtyris` where the 1962 has `Fe licis Martyris`; the 1862 reads `asstime` where the 1962 reads `assume` (letterforms inferred, not read: the difference is at the level of the recogniser); the 1862 reads `perp6tuum` where the 1962 reads `perpetuum` (letterforms inferred, not read: the difference is at the level of the recogniser); the 1862 reads `trfbue` where the 1962 reads `tribue` (letterforms inferred, not read: the difference is at the level of the recogniser); the 1862 reads `subsfdium Posteommunio de` where the 1962 reads `subsidium Per Dominum`; 5 further place(s) differ only in orthography, ligature or the recogniser's letterforms; the 1862 prints no conclusion at this place; the 1962 prints `Per Dominum`; the 1922 Mame reads `Secreta OsTIAS` where the 1962 reads `Hostias`; the 1922 Mame reads `méritis` where the 1962 reads `mentis` (letterforms inferred, not read: the difference is at the level of the recogniser); 2 further place(s) differ only in orthography, ligature or the recogniser's letterforms; the 1922 Mame prints no conclusion at this place; the 1962 prints `Per Dominum`. Corroboration: 1922 Tours Mame, printed p. 503 (artifact PDF p. 617), target-body character coverage 0.98, found by a sweep; Benziger 1962 conformed printing, target-body character coverage 0.84.
